- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak at 1.5x recent high or adjust downward by 2–5% after spike.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.10) over last 5–7 days, model often underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to avoid underreaction.
- Model frequently underestimates in early horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply slight upward bias (0.5–1.5%) to first 3–5 days.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion after strong trend, model often fails to correct; apply downward bias of 0.5–2% in next 3–5 days if sentiment turns neutral or negative.
- When sentiment history shows repeated small negative swings, model tends to lag; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to match sentiment momentum.
